newsitem.title: GERMANY: Frankfurt bourse closes firmer after U.S. election.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt bourse closes firmer after U.S. election.

text.p: The Frankfurt bourse ended sharply higher on Wednesday after Bill Clinton held onto the U.S. Presidency and the Republicans maintained control of Congress, a combination markets saw as optimal.
The DAX index of 30 leading shares, closed up 37.90 points, or 1.41 percent at 2,729.19, but off the day's highs and below the all-time bourse high of 2,739.26 hit on October 18.
The IBIS DAX, which measures all-day electronic dealings in the DAX index, made further gains after the floor close to end up 19.12 points at 2,735.28, as Wall Street opened firmer.
Post-bourse DAX gains would have been stronger had it not been for heavy losses by shares in German electronics firm Siemens, which lost almost nine percent to end down 7.17 marks at 72.80 marks.
The sell-off, with nearly 12 million shares changing hands, was prompted after Siemens said it did not expect improved results for the 1996/97 financial year.
Although the U.S. election results provided the main focus during bourse trade, the market was also kept busy digesting a barrage of company figures and news.
Chemical company Hoechst ended busy IBIS dealings up 2.53 marks, or over four percent, at 60.87 marks, after the company's nine month results were well received.
Competing chemical companies BASF AG and Bayer AG were pulled up by Hoechst's success. BASF was up 75 pfennigs at 51.25 marks in IBIS dealings, while Bayer climbed 88 pfennigs to 58.82 marks.
Preference shares in business software group SAP AG gained the most ground amongst the DAX stocks, continuing to recover from the blow of a profit warning two weeks ago.
SAP preference shares ended bourse dealings up over five percent, or 10.70 marks, at 208.20 marks.

Industrial group Daimler Benz AG also climbed strongly, after a newsletter said the firm was due to report nine-month turnover growth of 10 percent on Thursday. Daimler ended computer trade up 1.40 marks at 93.70 marks.
